correctness.rationale: For any integer \(p\ge2\) the explicitly defined set is symmetric, open and has \(\le7\) intervals. Exact membership is certified for every p by the separation of included even numerators from excluded odd numerators. The distinct orbit \(1/q,2^{p-1}/q,\ldots,2/q\) closes because the only selected affine maps are \((x+1)/2\) once and \(x/2\) otherwise; its first return slope is exactly \(2^{-p}\). All itinerary tests have boundary margin \(\ge1/(4q)\), giving open local basins, attracting stability and persistence. The arXiv source theorem gives the needed no-orbit conclusion for zero/one stubborn agent under the same symmetry/interior conditions. Replaying embedded verify.py with exact Fraction arithmetic returns VERIFY_OK for \(2\le p\le200\), which is supplemental to the infinite algebraic proof.

originality.rationale: The initiating 2024 primary full text states the three-agent two-stubborn period-three example, not arbitrarily prescribed least periods, a uniformly bounded number of interval components, local attraction or perturbative survival. Those are separately proved here; its convergence theorem covers only homogeneous stubborn opinions. Later norm-ball treatments address connected convex confidence geometry and cannot imply the stated disconnected-set construction. Targeted published-record and literature searches surfaced related examples but no implication covering the all-period theorem, subject to unindexed-work risk.
residual_risks: The complete 2025 CoDIT paper was not accessible as a verified full text; its known norm-ball scope appears inapplicable, but hidden discussion might cite a broader result.
An unindexed construction in piecewise-affine confidence or switched averaging dynamics could cover the same theorem despite unsuccessful targeted searches.
The construction is existential and uses p-dependent nonconvex confidence sets; it does not establish period universality for a fixed confidence set.

value.rationale: The 2024 initiating article explicitly asks when stubborn agents can cause oscillations and provides only a concrete period-three example. An all-integer primitive-period realization with a strict attraction multiplier and an interval-complexity budget independent of period is a substantive structural boundary: simple deterministic symmetric averaging with the minimal three agents can support robust periodic dynamics of unbounded temporal complexity. This is not merely renaming the period-three example, an arbitrary finite census or a routine numerical confirmation. The nonconvexity requirement and the dependence of the confidence set on p delimit the significance.
